entities.summary: Bulgaria is a sovereign nation in Eastern Europe, Europe. Its capital is Sofia. Official languages include Bulgarian. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic. Population: approximately 6.4 million. Area: 110,879 km². Comprehensive index for Bulgaria covering Thracian civilisation, First Bulgarian Empire 681 (Asparuh, Danube Bulgars + Slavs), Khan Krum/Simeon the Great (Golden Age, 893-927), Cyrillic alphabet (created by Saints Cyril and Methodius's disciples, Preslav/Ohrid), Second Bulgarian Empire (1185-1396), Ottoman conquest 1396 (~500 years), April Uprising 1876, Russo-Turkish War 1877-78 (liberation), Treaty of San Stefano/Berlin 1878, Balkan Wars 1912-13, WWI/WWII (Axis ally), Communist era 1944-89 (Todor Zhivkov 35 years), transition to democracy 1989, EU accession 2007.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bulgaria played a significant role in shaping Eastern European history, particularly during its Golden Age under Khan Krum and Simeon the Great (893-927), which saw the introduction of the Cyrillic alphabet. The country's modern independence was re-established after World War II, with EU accession in 2007 marking a new era of global integration.
